meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'If my mind can conceive it and my heart can believe it, then I can achieve it'?
meta.ogDescription: Not really Muhammad Ali — the wording traces to Jesse Jackson (1978) and Napoleon Hill’s ‘conceive and believe’ maxim.

answer.label: Not Muhammad Ali — a paraphrase of Jesse Jackson’s line
answer.sourceLine: The distinctive “my heart can believe it” framing was spoken by Jesse Jackson in a 1978 speech — “if my mind can conceive it and my heart can believe it, then I know I can achieve it because I am somebody” — itself built on Napoleon Hill’s older “conceive and believe” maxim. The trimmed version credited to Muhammad Ali only appears from 2001 onward, and Wikiquote files it under Misattributed.

source.heading: Where the line actually comes from
source.excerpt: If my mind can conceive it and my heart can believe it, then I know I can achieve it because I am somebody.
trail: The three-word “conceive … believe … achieve” formula was popularized by Napoleon Hill, whose 1937 “Think and Grow Rich” spoke of “anything the mind could conceive and believe” per Quote Investigator.
Quote Investigator traces the “my heart can believe it” wording to a 1978 Jesse Jackson speech and finds the Muhammad Ali credit only from 2001, calling it “only weak evidence.”
Wikiquote lists the line in its Misattributed section, noting it is “similar to a quote by Jesse Jackson, which is in turn a modification of a quote by Napoleon Hill.”
Quote sites and Ali collections such as Goodreads still print it under Ali’s name, which is how the misattribution keeps spreading.
source.excerptNote: Jesse Jackson’s 1978 wording, as documented by Quote Investigator. The line credited to Muhammad Ali drops “I know” and “because I am somebody.”

author.name: Jesse Jackson
author.heading: Whose words are these?
author.metaLine: b. 1941 · American civil-rights leader, Baptist minister & orator
author.bio: The Rev. Jesse Louis Jackson rose to prominence as an aide to Martin Luther King Jr. and became one of America’s most recognizable orators through his “I Am Somebody” refrain and two presidential campaigns. His 1978 rendering — “if my mind can conceive it and my heart can believe it, then I know I can achieve it” — is the closest documented source for the line now pinned on Muhammad Ali. Jackson himself was reworking a much older motivational maxim popularized by Napoleon Hill.

misattribution.heading: How Ali got the credit
misattribution.intro: This is a classic feel-good line that migrated onto a famous name. The wording is not original to Muhammad Ali — it is a trimmed version of a phrase Jesse Jackson used in 1978, which itself reworked Napoleon Hill.

items.scope: The exact “heart can believe it” wording
items.why: Quote Investigator documents Jackson saying “if my mind can conceive it and my heart can believe it, then I know I can achieve it because I am somebody” in a 1978 speech — the Ali version simply drops “I know” and “because I am somebody.”
Hill’s “Think and Grow Rich” popularized “anything the mind could conceive and believe,” per Quote Investigator; QI notes the broader motto is otherwise anonymous.

items.who: A 2001 newspaper columnist, then quote sites
items.why: The earliest link to Ali is a 2001 Wisconsin column; Wikiquote lists it as Misattributed, while sites like Goodreads keep printing it under his name.

misattribution.truthLine: No documented Ali speech, interview, or letter originates this line; the closest real source is Jesse Jackson’s 1978 wording, built on Napoleon Hill’s maxim.

context.heading: Why the mix-up sticks
lead: The saying belongs to a family of American self-help mantras built on three verbs — conceive, believe, achieve. Napoleon Hill packaged the idea for a mass audience in the 1930s, and preachers and motivational speakers reshaped it for decades after. Jesse Jackson’s cadenced 1978 version added the “heart” and the “I am somebody” refrain that make this phrasing memorable.

Muhammad Ali was a magnet for exactly this kind of aspirational one-liner, so a maxim already floating through motivational culture was easy to re-tag with his name once a columnist did so in 2001. The polish of the line, not any documented Ali source, is what keeps it attached to him.
context.pull: Conceive, believe, achieve — a self-help mantra, re-tagged with a champion’s name.
